clue.text: Kidnap seaman by canal

blocks.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
a canal in anatomy is a duct or tube

explanation.surface: A sailor is snatched away somewhere beside a canal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canal' looks like a waterway but here is the body's sense, a tube carrying fluid.
explanation.definitionFit: To abduct someone is to carry them off by force, which is exactly what kidnapping means.

clue.text: Last, in spite of expectations

blocks.note: first meaning: coming after every other one
second meaning: nevertheless, contrary to what was thought

explanation.walkthrough: Literally the phrase means following everybody else; idiomatically it means despite what was expected.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken word by word the phrase means following everyone, i.e. final, while as an idiom it means nevertheless.

clue.text: Small drop to drink before opening of Ayckbourn play

indicators.note: the opening of a word is where it starts, its first letter

blocks.note: a dram is a small measure of spirits
first letter of Ayckbourn

explanation.surface: A quick whisky before the first night of an Alan Ayckbourn comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' just puts one piece ahead of the next. Alan Ayckbourn is a prolific English playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a play written for the stage, so the noun play fits.

clue.text: Conspirator has wine brought round rear of chateau

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its back end, its last letter
brought round something means wrapped about it, enclosing it

blocks.note: cassis is a blackcurrant liqueur, and also a white wine from Provence
last letter of chateau

explanation.surface: A plotter gets wine carried round to the back of a French castle.
explanation.walkthrough: Cassius was a leader of the plot to assassinate Julius Caesar.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaius Cassius Longinus led the conspiracy to murder Julius Caesar, so he is the archetypal conspirator.

clue.text: Fainting quickly seizing wife having gin cocktail

indicators.note: to seize something is to grab hold of it, so the first word wraps around the second
a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of the word before it are mixed up

blocks.note: soon means before long, quickly
W is the standard abbreviation for wife
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone keels over fast after grabbing the spouse and downing a gin cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cocktail' reads as a drink, but it only tells you to mix the three letters before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Swooning is an older word for passing out or losing consciousness briefly, so it matches fainting.

clue.text: Actor in Duck Soup finally brought in after change

indicators.note: finally points to the end of the word, its last letter
something brought in is placed inside, here inside the bird

blocks.note: a widgeon (or wigeon) is a type of duck
to alter is to change
last letter of soup

explanation.surface: An actor appearing in the Marx Brothers film Duck Soup.
explanation.walkthrough: In the duck's name, P is inserted after ALTER, both going in just after its W. 'Duck Soup' looks like the film title, but it splits into a bird and a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Pidgeon was a Canadian-born Hollywood star of films such as Mrs Miniver, so he is an actor.

clue.text: Propane exploded? In theory

indicators.note: something exploded is blown apart, so its letters land in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be blown apart

explanation.surface: Did the gas cylinder blow up? Well, theoretically.
explanation.definitionFit: Something true on paper holds in principle or in writing but may not in practice, i.e. theoretically.

clue.text: Bury one in a US city among other things

indicators.note: one item in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: to inter is to bury
taken as written
LA is Los Angeles
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An instruction to bury someone in an American city, among other matters.
explanation.walkthrough: The Roman numeral for one goes inside Los Angeles's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Inter alia is a Latin phrase used in English meaning among other things.

clue.text: Forms army officer left out

indicators.note: something left out is omitted, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: a general is a senior army officer
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Paperwork for an army officer has been excluded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' does double duty here: it supplies the letter and with 'out' says to remove it.
explanation.definitionFit: Genera, the plural of genus, are categories or kinds in biology, so they are forms or types.

clue.text: Fungus and natterjacks, say, also found by lake

blocks.note: natterjacks are a species of toad, 'say' marking them as an example
too means also
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A mushroom and some toads are spotted together near the water.
explanation.walkthrough: The natterjack is a European toad living in sandy places.
explanation.definitionFit: A toadstool is a mushroom-like growth, usually poisonous, so it is a kind of fungus.

clue.text: Apparently some of those climbing the Eiger may be seen here

definitions.text: some of those climbing the Eiger may be seen here

blocks.note: first meaning: judging by appearances

blocks.clueFragment: some of those climbing the Eiger may be seen here
blocks.note: second meaning, literal: climbers can be found on the mountain's famous north wall

explanation.walkthrough: The Eiger is a Swiss Alpine peak whose north wall is a notorious climb, so mountaineers are literally on the face of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means judging by surface appearance, i.e. apparently, while literally describing climbers on a mountain's wall.

clue.text: Introduce Russian president

blocks.note: first meaning: to insert or put something into place
second meaning: the surname of Vladimir, Russia's leader

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests presenting a head of state to someone; instead the two words are separate meanings of one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something in is to insert or introduce it, and the same letters spell the Russian leader's surname.

clue.text: One's employed during high alert, no Walter Mitty?

indicators.note: someone high is intoxicated and out of order, so the letters of the next word are scrambled
being used during something places it in the middle of that thing

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
one is I, and the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A sober type is needed during a state of high alert, not a daydreamer.
explanation.walkthrough: Walter Mitty is James Thurber's fantasist who daydreams of heroics; his opposite is a person who sees things as they are.
explanation.definitionFit: A realist faces facts, the very opposite of a dreamer lost in fantasy like Thurber's character.

clue.text: Salesman in capital turned back to get a ruler

indicators.note: one thing being inside another means it is placed within it
something turned back faces the other way, so the combination is read from its end

blocks.note: Rome is the capital of Italy
a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: A travelling salesman in a capital city heads back to fetch a measuring stick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruler' tempts as a measuring stick, but it means a sovereign; the capital here is Italy's.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor is a sovereign who rules over an empire, so he is a ruler.

clue.text: Millions in petrodollars confused certain peers

indicators.note: something in another word is placed among its letters
confused things are jumbled up, so the letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for million
taken as written, to be mixed up

explanation.surface: Peers of the realm are baffled by millions in oil money.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lords Temporal are the hereditary and life peers in Britain's House of Lords, as distinct from the bishops, the Lords Spiritual.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lords Temporal are the secular members of the House of Lords, so they are a particular group of peers.

clue.text: Respect judge touring North Carolina

indicators.note: someone touring a place goes all round it, so one word surrounds the other

blocks.note: a referee judges a game
NC is the postal abbreviation for North Carolina

explanation.surface: A judge earns esteem on a trip around a US state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Respect' suggests esteem, but it is the sense in 'with respect to', i.e. relation.
explanation.definitionFit: In phrases like 'in respect of' and 'with reference to', the two nouns both mean relation or regard.

clue.text: Strong macho chaps quarantined by doctor

indicators.note: those quarantined are shut away inside, so these words are enclosed by the next

blocks.note: a vet is an animal doctor
he-men are tough macho men

explanation.surface: Tough guys isolated by a doctor in a medical quarantine.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehement feelings or arguments are forceful and intense, so the word means strong.

clue.text: Honest description of old-fashioned blonde?

blocks.note: first meaning: just and above board
second meaning: a blonde is light-haired, and someone old-fashioned is conventional and dull

explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the phrase describes a person both light-haired and behind the times: a fair-haired square.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means honest and without cheating, while its two halves separately mean light-haired and conventional.

clue.text: Failed to notice eroding ground

indicators.note: ground means crushed into pieces, so the letters are broken and reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written, to be crushed and remade

explanation.surface: Someone missed that the soil was wearing away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' reads as the noun for soil, but it is the past tense of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: To have ignored something is to have paid it no attention, failing to notice or heed it.

clue.text: Find fault with one of 007's allies

blocks.note: first meaning: to object or take issue
second meaning: the Cayman Islands boatman who helps James Bond in Dr No

explanation.walkthrough: 007 is James Bond; in Ian Fleming's Live and Let Die and Dr No his helper is a fisherman of this name.
explanation.definitionFit: To quarrel with something is to object to it or take issue, and it is also the name of Bond's Caribbean helper.

clue.text: Trouble had sprung up in plant

indicators.note: in a down clue, springing up means the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
taken as written

explanation.surface: Trouble had suddenly appeared in a plant, like a factory problem.
explanation.definitionFit: The dahlia is a garden flower with showy blooms grown from tubers, so it is a plant.

clue.text: Set out from Scottish island, extremely game

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the very ends of the word that follows

blocks.note: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde
first and last letters of game

explanation.surface: Someone sets off from a Scottish island, very much up for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set out' looks like setting off on a journey, but it means to lay things out.
explanation.definitionFit: To set out items is to lay them in order, which is what arranging means.

clue.text: Former partner, fairly large model

blocks.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
ample means generous in size

explanation.surface: Someone's ex was a rather large fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' suggests a catwalk, but here it means a pattern to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: An example is something held up as a pattern to copy, which is a model.

clue.text: Earlier convent not completed

indicators.note: something not completed lacks its ending, so its final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a priory is a religious house, such as a convent

explanation.surface: A convent's building work was never finished before.
explanation.definitionFit: Prior means coming before in time, so it is a synonym of earlier.

clue.text: Long narrow mark on river vessel

blocks.note: a line is a long thin mark
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A long thin streak is seen on a boat on the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A liner is a large passenger ship, so it is a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Freudians broadcast to get money for a good cause?

definitions.text: get money for a good cause

indicators.note: to broadcast seed is to scatter it widely, so the letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be scattered

explanation.surface: Followers of Freud go on air to collect money for charity.
explanation.definitionFit: To fundraise is to collect donations for a charity or similar worthy purpose.

clue.text: Story one cadet concocted

indicators.note: something concocted is made up by mixing ingredients, so the letters are mixed

blocks.note: taken as written, to be mixed

explanation.surface: A tale made up by a young officer trainee.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a short entertaining account of a real incident, so it is a story.

clue.text: Girl has little time for wine

blocks.note: Clare is a girl's name
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A young woman has hardly a moment to spare for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain claret is the usual name for red Bordeaux.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is red wine from the Bordeaux region of France.
